clue.text: It takes a seaman to make a tiptop land machine work

parts.note: tiptop means excellent, super
a car is a machine for travelling on land
to work, of a machine, is to go

explanation.surface: Someone needs a sailor's help to get a first-class motor vehicle running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It takes a' and 'to make a' are link words; the definition is 'seaman'.
explanation.definitionFit: A supercargo is a ship's officer who manages the cargo on board, so a seagoing hand.

clue.text: "Let not ambition mock their — toil" (Gray)

parts.words: Let not ambition mock their — toil
parts.note: fill the gap in a line of Thomas Gray's Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard

explanation.walkthrough: Gray's line is 'Let not Ambition mock their useful toil'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gray's Elegy praises the helpful, productive labour of humble villagers.

clue.text: Didn't he do well ? Far, from it

definitions.text: Didn't he do well ? Far, from it

parts.words: Didn't he do well ? Far, from it
parts.note: a cheer of praise turned round: this person did far from well, he did wrong

explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer, a sinner, is someone whose deeds are bad.

clue.text: The padding of yarns

parts.note: padding made from the raw stuff of two kinds of yarn, plant fibre and sheep's fleece

explanation.definitionFit: Cotton wool is soft padding, and its two words are both yarns.

clue.text: When the boss is on it, best butter his attendant

definitions.text: When the boss is on it

parts.note: a ram is the champion among butters, animals that butt
a page is a boy attendant

explanation.surface: Advice to flatter the manager's assistant when the manager is in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' is not flattery but one that butts; a boss 'on the rampage' is in a fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the rampage means storming about in a violent rage.

clue.text: But very often the start of a fairy-tale

definitions.text: But very often the start of a fairy-tale

parts.words: But very often the start of a fairy-tale
parts.note: a word meaning a single time, not often at all, which nevertheless opens fairy stories again and again

explanation.definitionFit: Fairy stories open 'upon a time' after this word, which itself means on one occasion only.

clue.text: Battered sea-chest passes to the Crown

indicators.note: battered means knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A damaged seaman's trunk is handed over to the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Property escheats when it reverts to the state, the Crown, for lack of an heir.

clue.text: Time of reckoning. "when mercy seasons justice"?

definitions.meaning: a day when rents and accounts fall due
Portia's line from The Merchant of Venice; quarter is mercy shown to a beaten enemy, so a day of such mercy

explanation.walkthrough: In England quarter days, such as Lady Day and Michaelmas, are traditional dates for paying rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarter days are the four days a year when rents are settled; quarter also means clemency.

clue.text: Try some of Edna's sausage rolls-they're capital

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are taken, a run spanning them

explanation.surface: An invitation to sample a friend's sausage rolls, which are praised as first-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'Edna's sausage'; 'rolls' and 'they're' are surface padding as link words, and 'capital' is not 'excellent' but a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nassau is the capital city of the Bahamas.

clue.text: Air items of difference one after another

indicators.note: letters that are 'of difference' have been made different, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Songs that are unlike each other are played in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Seriatim is Latin for in series, point by point in succession.

clue.text: Not always a practising orator ?

parts.note: the idea of someone who does not always practise what they preach: a speaker from the pulpit

explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman giving sermons is a public speaker, proverbially told to practise what he preaches.

clue.text: Addison's signed letters to a muse

definitions.meaning: Joseph Addison signed his Spectator essays with one of the four letters C, L, I or O
one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, the muse of history

explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Addison was an 18th-century English essayist who wrote for The Spectator.
explanation.definitionFit: Addison's essay signature spelt the name of the Muse of history, so one word covers both senses.

clue.text: Which county is named for India's governor-general ?

parts.note: Cornwall is a county in south-west England

explanation.surface: A question about which English shire bears the name of an Indian viceroy.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwallis is also famous for surrendering at Yorktown.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Cornwallis was Governor-General of India in the 1780s and 1790s.

clue.text: Fast-falling flower in an Alpine village

definitions.text: Fast-falling flower in an Alpine village

parts.words: Fast-falling flower in an Alpine village
parts.note: in a deep mountain valley the dark of evening comes down quickly, and that darkness of evening also names a poisonous plant

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast-falling' describes the shade of night in a valley village; 'flower' is the plant sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly nightshade is a flowering plant, and the shadow of evening falls quickly among high mountains.

clue.text: Dramatic way to tail the car, anyhow

indicators.note: anyhow means in any old way, in a jumble, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A showy method of following a car any way you can.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical means stagey, belonging to the theatre.

clue.text: Adverse criticism of a cloth cover ?

definitions.meaning: to proof a cloth cover again, making a raincoat waterproof once more

explanation.definitionFit: A reproof is a rebuke; read as re-proof it means treating fabric to be waterproof again.

clue.text: Ancient can enter force

indicators.note: one piece entering another goes inside it

parts.note: to prise is to force open
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: An old tin is jammed open with pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Pristine originally means of the earliest time, original and unspoilt.

clue.text: The fate of some kings Richard II wished to talk about

definitions.text: Richard II wished to talk about
definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's Richard II says 'let us sit upon the ground and tell sad stories of the death of kings

explanation.walkthrough: Deposed also means testified, so 'talk about' leans on that sense too.
explanation.definitionFit: Deposed means removed from the throne, the very word in Richard II's speech about the fates of kings.

clue.text: Like the cost of maintaining these power lines ?

definitions.text: Like the cost of maintaining these power lines ?

parts.words: Like the cost of maintaining these power lines
parts.note: running costs of a business, and cables carried on pylons above our heads, share one word

explanation.definitionFit: Running costs are overheads, and cables strung on pylons are aloft lines.

clue.text: Maxim in an acquired name

indicators.note: one piece set in another goes inside it

parts.note: a gnome is a pithy saying, a maxim

explanation.surface: A wise saying hidden within a nickname someone has earned.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnomen is an extra name added in Roman naming, like Africanus, earned by deeds.

clue.text: Illumination that struck the Spanish in our isle?

definitions.text: Illumination that struck the Spanish in our isle?

parts.words: Illumination that struck the Spanish in our isle
parts.note: a pale bright light, with its first word sounding like the Isle of Wight, off which the Spanish Armada was fought in 1588

explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Wight is an island off England's south coast; the Spanish Armada was engaged near it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary daylight is a mix of all colours, a pale radiance; the first word puns on Wight.

clue.text: Less virtuous type of virtue describes this clue

definitions.meaning: a woman 'of ... virtue' is one of loose morals
the clue is simple to solve

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'easy virtue' names loose morals, and the same adjective means simple, as this clue is.

clue.text: " That unhoped That men call age" (Brooke)

definitions.text: " That unhoped That men call age" (Brooke)

parts.words: That unhoped That men call age
parts.note: fill the gap in a line of Rupert Brooke's sonnet The Soldier-era poem The Dead

explanation.walkthrough: Brooke's sonnet The Dead reads 'That unhoped serene, that men call age'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brooke's dead soldiers gave up the calm, untroubled peace of old age.

clue.text: Not keen to meet a seaport seducer ?

parts.note: loth means reluctant, not keen
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian seaport

explanation.surface: A reluctant traveller meets a womaniser at a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lothario is a libertine, the rake of Rowe's play The Fair Penitent.

clue.text: A break perhaps, or what helps a player to make one

definitions.meaning: a pause is an example of a break

definitions.text: what helps a player to make one
definitions.meaning: in snooker a cue support helps a player build a scoring break

explanation.walkthrough: Snooker is a cue game popular in Britain; a break is a run of scoring shots.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause is a break from work, and in snooker the cue support is used when compiling a scoring break.

clue.text: Pisces-seen in the daylight sky

definitions.meaning: Latin for fishes, the zodiac sign
one dappled with rows of small cloud

explanation.definitionFit: This is a sea fish, and a sky of rippled cirrocumulus clouds is named after its striped back.

clue.text: They're surrounded by magpies

parts.note: on a shooting target the 'magpie' is the ring just outside the ring next to the bull

explanation.walkthrough: 'Magpies' are not birds here: in target shooting a magpie is a shot in a particular outer ring.
explanation.definitionFit: On a rifle target the rings nearest the bull are encircled by the magpie ring.

clue.text: Deceitful weaver's snarl

definitions.meaning: Scott: 'Oh what a ... we weave, when first we practise to deceive'

explanation.walkthrough: The line comes from Walter Scott's poem Marmion.
explanation.definitionFit: Scott's line on deception gives the phrase, and a knotted mass of threads is a literal snarl.
